evals.prompt: I've fixed the JVM compatibility bug in the dokka-convention plugin. The changes are staged. Commit them, push to origin, and open a PR against upstream main. My fork is at github.tools.sap/I062843/android-build and upstream is github.tools.sap/CloudAndroidSDK/android-build.
evals.expected_output: A commit with a clear why-focused message, branch pushed to origin with -u, a PR created against upstream with Summary + Test plan sections, the PR URL printed, and after ~60s the bot comments fetched and explained.
assertions: The commit message uses imperative form and explains the motivation (not just 'what changed')
git push uses the -u flag to set upstream tracking
gh pr create targets the upstream repo (not the fork)
The PR body contains a Summary section and a Test plan section
The PR URL is printed to the user
Bot comments are fetched after PR creation (gh pr view ... --comments)
Each bot finding is explained to the user with a recommendation

evals.prompt: commit and push my changes, then open a PR. I've already got a branch called fix/null-pointer-exception. origin is my fork, upstream is the org repo.
evals.expected_output: Runs git status + diff to understand what's staged, writes a targeted commit, pushes to origin, creates the PR against upstream, and reviews any bot feedback.
assertions: git status and git diff are run before committing
Only relevant files are staged (not git add -A blindly)
Commit message has a short subject line (<=72 chars)
PR is opened against upstream, not the user's fork
After PR creation, bot comments are retrieved and surfaced

evals.prompt: The PR bot left a comment on PR #14 saying we should use jvmToolchain instead of compilerOptions. Can you review what it said and address it?
evals.expected_output: Fetches the PR comments, identifies and explains the bot's finding, determines whether it's valid, applies the fix if valid, commits and pushes the follow-up, and confirms the PR is updated.
assertions: gh pr view is used to retrieve bot comments
The bot finding is explained clearly to the user
The validity of the finding is evaluated (not blindly accepted or rejected)
If valid, a fix is applied and committed
The updated branch is pushed so the PR reflects the fix
